See how you translated these names in 41:11.
See how you translated this phrase in 8:10.

2.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 37:2.
See how you translated the similar expression in 36:7.
See how you translated the similar expression in 26:13.

The expression **we are left** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [only a few of us remain from the many we once were]

The people are using **your eyes**, one part of Jeremiah, to represent Jeremiah himself as the one who is seeing them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [just as you yourself are seeing us]

3.q: וְ⁠יַגֶּד־לָ֨⁠נוּ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔י⁠ךָ אֶת־הַ⁠דֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נֵֽלֶךְ־בָּ֑⁠הּ וְ⁠אֶת־הַ⁠דָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר נַעֲשֶֽׂה
3.note: Here, **that** marks **Yahweh your God may declare to us the way in which we should walk and the word that we should do** as the goal or purpose of the people asking Jeremiah to pray for them in the previous verse. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose.

Jeremiah is using **the way in which we should walk** as a common expression of the culture to mean “where we should go.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly as in the UST.

4.note: **Behold me** is an expression that people of this culture would commonly use to mean that they were about to do something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Now I am about to pray to Yahweh your God]

4.q: וְֽ⁠הָיָ֡ה כָּֽל הַ⁠דָּבָר֩ אֲשֶׁר יַעֲנֶ֨ה יְהוָ֤ה אֶתְ⁠כֶם֙ אַגִּ֣יד לָ⁠כֶ֔ם
4.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about Jeremiah declaring the message before the information about **every word that Yahweh answers you**. Alternate translation: [And I will declare to you every word that Yahweh answers you]

Jeremiah is emphasizing a positive meaning by using a negative word, **not**, together with a mild expression that is the opposite of the intended meaning. He means that he will tell them everything that Yahweh says. If it would be helpful in your language, you could emphasize the positive meaning in a strong way. Alternate translation: [I will declare every single word to you]

5.note: Jeremiah is stating the pronoun **they** separately, even though the verb translated as **they said** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that it was the people themselves who made this solemn promise. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [Then it was the people themselves who said] or [Then they themselves said]

5.q: יְהִ֤י יְהוָה֙ בָּ֔⁠נוּ לְ⁠עֵ֖ד אֱמֶ֣ת וְ⁠נֶאֱמָ֑ן אִם־לֹ֡א כְּֽ⁠כָל־הַ֠⁠דָּבָר אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִֽשְׁלָחֲ⁠ךָ֜ יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֶ֛י⁠ךָ אֵלֵ֖י⁠נוּ כֵּ֥ן נַעֲשֶֽׂה
5.note: Following the custom of the culture, the people are swearing an oath by stating the first part of a condition (“if”) but not the second part (“then”). If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explicitly state the second part of this condition. Alternate translation: [May Yahweh be against us as a witness of truth and being faithful, and may he punish us severely if we fail to do according to every word which Yahweh your God sends you to tell us. Indeed]

The terms **truth** and **being faithful** mean similar things. The people are using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [as a completely reliable witness]

5.q: יְהִ֤י יְהוָה֙ בָּ֔⁠נוּ לְ⁠עֵ֖ד אֱמֶ֣ת וְ⁠נֶאֱמָ֑ן אִם־לֹ֡א כְּֽ⁠כָל־הַ֠⁠דָּבָר אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִֽשְׁלָחֲ⁠ךָ֜ יְהוָ֧ה & אֱלֹהֶ֛י⁠ךָ אֵלֵ֖י⁠נוּ כֵּ֥ן נַעֲשֶֽׂה
5.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **if not according to every word with which Yahweh your God sends you to us thus we do** before the information about **May Yahweh be against us as a witness of truth and being faithful**. Alternate translation: [If we do not do thus according to every word with which Yahweh your God sends you to us, may Yahweh be against us as a witness of truth and being faithful]

6.note: The people are referring to any answer that Yahweh might give by naming two major components, **good** and **bad**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Whatever Yahweh’s answer may be]

6.q: בְּ⁠ק֣וֹל יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֗י⁠נוּ & נִשְׁמָ֑ע & נִשְׁמַ֔ע בְּ⁠ק֖וֹל יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי⁠נוּ
6.note: Here, **voice** represents “what Yahweh says,” and **listen to** means “obey.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [we will obey the commands of Yahweh our God … we obey the commands of Yahweh our God]

7.note: Jeremiah is using the phrase translated as **Now it happened** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:9.

8.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 8:10.

9.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 21:4.

9.q: כֹּֽה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר שְׁלַחְתֶּ֤ם אֹתִ⁠י֙ אֵלָ֔י⁠ו לְ⁠הַפִּ֥יל תְּחִנַּתְ⁠כֶ֖ם לְ⁠פָנָֽי⁠ו
9.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh, the God of Israel, to whom you sent me to present your humble request, says that]
See how you translated the similar expression “Perhaps their supplication will fall to the face of Yahweh” in 36:7.

10.note: Yahweh is using the two similar-sounding Hebrew verb forms translated as **turning** and **dwell** together in order to intensify his expression of the idea that they convey. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [If you will indeed stay]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people were a building that he could **build** or **tear down**. It means that he will make them strong as a nation and will not destroy them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [then I will make you prosper as a nation and I will not ruin you]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people were a plant that he could **plant** or **uproot**. It means that he will settle them securely in the land and will not remove them from it. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will settle you securely in the land and I will not remove you from it]
See how you translated the similar expression in 26:13.

11.q: אַל־תִּֽירְא֗וּ מִ⁠פְּנֵי֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל אֲשֶׁר־אַתֶּ֥ם יְרֵאִ֖ים מִ⁠פָּנָ֑י⁠ו
11.note: Jeremiah is using **from the face of** as a common expression of the culture to mean “because of” or “on account of” and he is using “from whose face” as a common expression of the culture to mean “on account of whose presence.” If these phrase does not have these meaning for your readers, you could use comparable expressions from your language that do have that meaning, or you could state the meanings plainly. Alternate translation: [You shall not fear the king of Babylon, whom you are afraid of]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:8.

Yahweh is using **I am with you** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I will help and protect you.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [for I will help and protect you]
Here, **hand** represents “power” or “control.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from his power]

12.note: Yahweh is using **I will give to you compassions** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I will cause someone to show mercy to you.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will cause you to receive mercy]
The pronoun **he** refers to the king of Babylon, not to Yahweh, who is speaking. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the king of Babylon will have compassion]

13.q: וְ⁠אִם אֹמְרִ֣ים אַתֶּ֔ם לֹ֥א נֵשֵׁ֖ב בָּ⁠אָ֣רֶץ הַ⁠זֹּ֑את
13.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [But if you are saying that you will not dwell in this land]
See how you translated the similar expression in 26:13.

14.note: Here, **the sound of a shofar** represents “war,” since soldiers blew a shofar to warn of an attack or to call soldiers to battle. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and we will not be called to battle]

The people are using **bread**, one kind of food, to represent food in general. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and we will not go hungry for lack of food] or [and we will not go hungry because of lack of food]

15.note: The words **then now, therefore** introduce the consequence of what the people would be saying, as Jeremiah described in the previous two verses. If the connection between this statement and the previous one is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word or words to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [if that is what you choose to say, then now] or [if that is how you choose to respond, then now
See how you translated the similar expression in 2:4.

15.q: כֹּֽה אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אִם אַ֠תֶּם שׂ֣וֹם תְּשִׂמ֤וּ⁠ן פְּנֵי⁠כֶם֙ לָ⁠בֹ֣א מִצְרַ֔יִם
15.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says that if setting you will set your faces to go to Egypt]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **set** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [If you are determined to set]

Yahweh is using **set your faces** as a common expression of the culture to mean “firmly decide.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [If indeed you firmly decide]

16.q: הַ⁠חֶ֗רֶב אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתֶּם֙ יְרֵאִ֣ים מִמֶּ֔⁠נָּה שָׁ֛ם תַּשִּׂ֥יג אֶתְ⁠כֶ֖ם בְּ⁠אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְ⁠הָ⁠רָעָ֞ב אֲשֶׁר־אַתֶּ֣ם דֹּאֲגִ֣ים מִמֶּ֗⁠נּוּ שָׁ֣ם יִדְבַּ֧ק אַחֲרֵי⁠כֶ֛ם מִצְרַ֖יִם
16.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **the sword that you are afraid of** with the information **it will overtake you in the land of Egypt** and you may want to put the information about **the famine that you are anxious about** with the information **it will cling after you**. Alternate translation: [the sword that you are afraid of will overtake you there in the land of Egypt and the famine that you are anxious about, it will cling after you there to Egypt]
Here, **the sword** represents “war.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the warfare]

16.q: וְ⁠הָ⁠רָעָ֞ב אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּ֣ם דֹּאֲגִ֣ים מִמֶּ֗⁠נּוּ שָׁ֣ם יִדְבַּ֧ק אַחֲרֵי⁠כֶ֛ם מִצְרַ֖יִם
16.note: Yahweh is speaking of **the famine** as if it were a living thing that could **cling after** the Judeans and follow them to Egypt. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the famine that you are anxious about will also be severe there in Egypt, where you will go]

17.note: Here the masculine term **men** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [all the people]
See how you translated the similar expression in 42:15. Alternate translation: [resolve] or [firmly decide]
See how you translated the similar expression in 14:12.

The terms **survivor** and **fugitive** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis to show that no one at all will escape. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [anyone at all who gets away alive]

17.q: מִ⁠פְּנֵי֙ הָֽ⁠רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י מֵבִ֥יא עֲלֵי⁠הֶֽם
17.note: Yahweh is using **from the face of** as a common expression of the culture to mean “because of” or “on account of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [because of the disaster that I am bringing upon them]

18.q: כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁר֩ נִתַּ֨ךְ אַפִּ֜⁠י וַ⁠חֲמָתִ֗⁠י עַל יֹֽשְׁבֵי֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם כֵּ֣ן תִּתַּ֤ךְ חֲמָתִ⁠י֙ עֲלֵי⁠כֶ֔ם
18.note: See how you translated the similar phrase “my nose and my heat will be poured out” in 7:20. Alternate translation: [Just as I punished the dwellers of Jerusalem severely because of my fierce anger, so I will punish you severely because of my anger]

18.q: נִתַּ֨ךְ אַפִּ֜⁠י וַ⁠חֲמָתִ֗⁠י עַל־יֹֽשְׁבֵי֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם כֵּ֣ן תִּתַּ֤ךְ חֲמָתִ⁠י֙
18.note: The expressions **were poured out** and **will be poured out** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, Yahweh did it. Alternate translation: [I poured out my anger and my wrath on the dwellers of Jerusalem, so I will pour out my heat]

Here, **execration**, **horror**, **curse**, and **taunt** represent the people as the objects of these things. It means that people will use their name when cursing others, will be horrified at what happens to them, and will insult them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And people will use your name as a curse, they will be horrified at what happens to you, they will use your name when they pronounce curses, and they will mock you]

19.q: דִּבֶּ֨ר יְהוָ֤ה עֲלֵי⁠כֶם֙ שְׁאֵרִ֣ית יְהוּדָ֔ה אַל תָּבֹ֖אוּ מִצְרָ֑יִם
19.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh has told you, remnant of Judah, that you must not go to Egypt.]
See how you translated this phrase in 26:15.

The pronoun **I** could refer to: (1) Jeremiah, who is speaking to the people and who goes on to say “I have declared it to you today” in verse 21. Alternate translation: [I, Jeremiah, have given a warning to you today] (2) Yahweh, whose words Jeremiah has just quoted. Alternate translation: [Yahweh have given a warning to you today]

20.note: The phrase **you have gone astray** follows a correction in the margin of the text that Hebrew scribes have recommended. The standard written Hebrew text as we have it today spells this word in a way that is difficult to understand here. The correction fits the context better, since Jeremiah is speaking to the people about what they themselves have done. You may want to follow this correction in your translation, or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [you have led yourselves astray]

Jeremiah is using **you have gone astray at your lives** as a common expression of the culture. Here it could mean: (1) “you have gone astray at the cost of your lives.” Alternate translation: [you have made a mistake that will cost you your lives] (2) that the Judeans had gone astray in their “souls” or “inner selves” because the Hebrew word translated as “at your lives” could be translated “in your souls.” Alternate translation: [you deceived yourselves] or [you were insincere]

Jeremiah is stating the pronoun **you** separately, even though the verb translated as **you sent** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that it was the people themselves who had asked him to go to Yahweh for them. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [it was you who sent me]

20.q: לֵ⁠אמֹ֔ר הִתְפַּלֵּ֣ל בַּעֲדֵ֔⁠נוּ אֶל יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֑י⁠נוּ וּ⁠כְ⁠כֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֹאמַ֜ר יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵ֛י⁠נוּ כֵּ֥ן הַגֶּד לָ֖⁠נוּ וְ⁠עָשִֽׂינוּ
20.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [asking me to pray on behalf of you to Yahweh your God and, according to all that Yahweh your God says, to declare it to you, and saying that you will do it]

21.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 26:5.

Jeremiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and you have not listened to all that he sent me to say to you]
See how you translated the similar expression in 9:13.

22.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 26:15.
See how you translated the similar expression in 14:12.
It might seem that the expression **there** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [to sojourn]
